To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) erythrocyte (Ery) and muscle (Mus) acetylcholineterase (ACh) are comparably inhibited by organophosphates (OP) in vitro, (ii) Ery and Mus AChE are comparably reactivated in vitro, (iii) oximes reactivating OP-inhibited erythrocyte acetylcholinetransferase (Ery AChE) are also reactivating OP inhibited muscle AChE

(1) the in vitro model is an excellent tool to study the kinetics of oxime reactivation of OP-inhibited AChE, (2) the model is versatile, since it can be applied to different species, (3) erythrocyte is a good surrogate of muscle AChE, and (4) there are species-specific differences in the kinetics of OP inhibition and oxime reactivation.
the reactivation of OP-inhibited human erythrocyte or muscle AChE can be studied in an in vitro model with continuous real-time monitoring of membrane-bound enzyme activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an in vitro assay system to investigate the reactivation kinetics of organophosphorus-inhibited AChE.
the development of new therapeutic approaches for the treatment of organophosphorus compound poisoning and the optimization of existing ones.
the development of an innovative, versatile and promising in vitro assay for the investigation of oxime-induced AChE reactivation in OP-poisoned patients and in therapeutic animal models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the oxime-induced reactivator kinetics of OP-inactivated erythrocyte or muscle AChE is species dependent and that erythrocytes can be used to predict oxime-induced reactivity of muscle AChE, provided that the same animal species is used for both studies.

the erythrocyte model is suitable for the investigation of the oxime-induced re-activation of OP-inhibited erythrocyte but not muscle AChE in different animal species, and that the erythroeyte model should be used with great caution when extrapolating the findings to synaptic AChE.

oxime reactivation of AChE is a complex process and that the kinetics of oxime-induced-reactivation of OP-inhibited AChE is not only determined by the OP-inhibitor and oxime used, but also by the animal species.

the dynamic in vitro model is a very promising model for future investigations of oxime-induced AChE reactivation kinetics in various species.
the in vitro assay with immobilized erythrocyte or muscle AChE is a very useful tool for the investigation of OP-induced toxicity in different animal species.
the in vitro assay with erythrocyte or muscle AChE is a very useful and versatile model for the study of the reactivation kinetics of AChE from various species.

the in vitro model with on-line determination of AChE activity is a powerful tool for comparative analysis of OP-inhibition and reactivation of AChE.

a dynamic in vitro model with continuous real-time determination of AChE activity is a versatile and promising model for the investigation of oxime-induced AChE reactivation kinetics of various animal species.
